current_disclosures.section: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry
current_disclosures.summary: Micron faces technological barriers to meeting long-term customer needs, including achieving acceptable yields for HBM with multiple chip layers, limitations on 3D stacking, improving power consumption, and shrinking product sizes at historical rates. While the company invests in R&D for technologies like EUV lithography, these new technologies add complexity, schedule risks, and may prevent recovery of R&D investments or realization of economic benefits from density increases.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks in New Product Development and AI Execution
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces intense competition and rapid technological change in the AI market, with significant risks related to developing, qualifying, and shipping new products on time. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, while uncertainty in long-term AI adoption and potential failure to achieve return on investment pose material risks. The company cannot guarantee success against competitors like Nvidia or customers developing internal solutions, and product complexity necessitates successful high-value launches to maintain average selling prices and competitive positioning.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies face risks from rapid technological change leading to shortened product life cycles and competitive disadvantages if they fail to innovate. Micron highlights the risk of competitors developing superior technologies that create cost or performance advantages (mu_2024_1A_P024_S007, mu_2024_1A_P027_S007), while AMD emphasizes that failure to develop or ship new products on time may cause a loss of competitive positioning and require price discounts (amd_2024_1A_P024_S004, amd_2024_1A_P024_S005). Both disclosures stress the difficulty of ensuring new technologies are well-received or successful despite substantial R&D investments (mu_2024_1A_P027_S002 vs amd_2024_1A_P024_S005).

sentences.text: If competitors are more successful at developing or implementing new product or process technology, their products could have cost or performance advantages.
Our competitors are working to develop new memory and storage technologies that may offer performance and/or cost advantages to existing technologies and render existing technologies obsolete.

If we fail to or are delayed in identifying, developing, qualifying or shipping new products or technologies that provide value to our customers and address these new trends, or if we fail to predict which new form factors, product features preferences or requirements consumers will adopt and adapt our business accordingly, we may lose competitive positioning, which could cause us to lose market share and require us to discount the selling prices of our products.

Although we make substantial investments in research and development, we cannot be certain that we will be able to develop, obtain or successfully implement new products and technologies on a timely basis or that they will be well-received by our customers.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Investment Risks and AI Technology Development
comparisons.peer_summary: Significant investments in research and development carry the risk of slow or unsuccessful returns, particularly in developing advanced technologies like custom AI accelerators and XPUs; failure to timely develop these or focus on non-adopted technologies could impair competitive position and negatively impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose risks that failure to timely develop advanced technologies could impair their competitive position and lead to obsolescence of existing products. Micron cites competitors working to develop technologies that may render existing technologies obsolete (mu_2024_1A_P027_S007), while Avago warns that failure to successfully develop increasingly advanced technologies, including custom AI accelerators, could impair its competitive position and that focusing on non-adopted technologies may reduce demand (avgo_2024_1A_P044_S003, avgo_2024_1A_P044_S005). Both link these technological development risks directly to competitive standing and product viability.

sentences.text: Our competitors are working to develop new memory and storage technologies that may offer performance and/or cost advantages to existing technologies and render existing technologies obsolete.
Failure to successfully develop increasingly advanced technologies, including ASICs such as custom AI accelerators or XPUs and other AI-related products, could impair our competitive position.

If we fail to timely develop new and enhanced products and technologies, if we focus on technologies that do not become widely adopted, or if new competitive technologies that we do not support become widely accepted, demand for our products such as our custom AI accelerators or XPUs and other AI-related products may be reduced.

comparisons.peer_summary: Risks in developing next-generation nodes include timing delays, lower yields, and higher costs due to advanced equipment. Delays can cause missed customer design windows, larger die sizes, and supply constraints, while new nodes typically have higher depreciation and lower yields than mature nodes.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify specific technical barriers to technology advancement, including yield challenges. Micron notes barriers such as achieving acceptable yields for HBM and limitations on 3D memory layers (mu_2024_1A_P027_S002), while Intel explicitly lists lower-than-anticipated manufacturing yields and timing delays as inherent risks in developing next-generation process technologies (intc_2024_1A_P015_S001, intc_2024_1A_P015_S004). Intel further notes that increased complexity and larger die sizes make processes more susceptible to defects and lower yields (intc_2024_1A_P015_S007), paralleling Micron's focus on the physical and yield-related difficulties of advanced memory structures.

sentences.text: These barriers include achieving acceptable yields and quality for HBM products with their multiple memory chip layers, potential limitations on stacking additional 3D memory layers, increasing bits per cell (i.e., cell levels), meeting higher density requirements, developing advanced packaging solutions, improving power consumption and reliability, and delivering advanced features and higher performance.

Risks inherent in the development of next-generation process technologies include production timing delays, lower-than-anticipated manufacturing yields, longer manufacturing throughput times, failure to achieve expected performance, power, and area improvements, and product defects and errata (deviations from published specifications).

As the die size of our products has increased and our manufacturing process nodes have increased the number of transistors per die, our products and manufacturing processes have grown increasingly complex and more susceptible to product defects and errata, which at times also contribute to production timing delays and lower yields that may also increase our costs to manufacture and warranty our products.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of failing to adapt to industry and market changes
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's accelerated computing platforms face rapid technological and customer requirement changes, creating a risk that failure to identify these changes, adapt strategies, or maintain product compatibility may adversely impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies warn that rapid technological and industry changes create risks if they fail to adapt strategies and develop compatible or superior new products. Micron states that rapid technological change could contribute to shortened product life cycles and that competitor success could lead to advantages for them (mu_2024_1A_P024_S006, mu_2024_1A_P024_S007). Similarly, NVIDIA warns that its platforms experience rapid changes in technology and standards, and failure to timely identify these changes or adapt strategies could adversely impact financial results (nvda_2024_1A_P007_S001, nvda_2024_1A_P008_S002).

sentences.text: Additionally, rapid technological change in markets we serve could contribute to shortened product life cycles and a decline in average selling prices of our products.

Our accelerated computing platforms experience rapid changes in technology, customer requirements, competitive products, and industry standards.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of rapid technological change and competition
comparisons.peer_summary: Intense competition in a rapidly changing industry may lead to decreased demand for products and technologies or declining average selling prices for Qualcomm and its customers.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify intense competition in a rapidly changing environment as a risk that can lead to declining average selling prices and reduced demand. Micron explicitly links rapid technological change to a decline in average selling prices of products (mu_2024_1A_P024_S006). Qualcomm similarly states that the environment of rapid technological change and intense competition could result in declining average selling prices for its products (qcom_2024_1A_P087_S001, qcom_2024_1A_P087_S002).

sentences.text: Additionally, rapid technological change in markets we serve could contribute to shortened product life cycles and a decline in average selling prices of our products.
Our industry is subject to intense competition in an environment of rapid technological change.

Our success depends in part on our ability to adapt to such change and compete effectively; and such change and competition could result in decreased demand for our products and technologies or declining average selling prices for our products or those of our customers or licensees.
